title: How Large Language Models Systematically Misrepresent American Climate Opinions
findings: LLMs tend to overestimate the climate concern of religious individuals compared to non-religious individuals. This overestimation was statistically significant overall and particularly pronounced for Black, Hispanic, and 'Other' non-Hispanic respondents, while not being statistically significant for White respondents.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured the effect of religiosity, coded as a binary variable (religious vs. not religious), on the gap between Large Language Model (LLM) predictions and actual human survey responses regarding climate change opinions.
